reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes StrongBlock nodes as a route to passive income using reported earnings, projected returns, and compounding examples. It instructs viewers to buy STRONG, transfer tokens to a wallet, fund ETH gas, and pay recurring maintenance fees, while linking node participation to a non-refundable contribution and ongoing payment. The speaker acknowledges volatility and includes a disclaimer, but the promotion still presents increasingly large dollar outcomes tied to creating more nodes.

this strong block has made it possible for anyone to create a node in seconds and receive strong token rewards every single day
you have to pay a monthly maintenance fee to keep your node running which is 1495 and that's every single month
you have to pay the $14.95 fee, you have to pay gas fees to create the node
we get rewarded about three strong coins per month per node that we create

opening.argument: The presentation repeatedly qualifies its projections instead of guaranteeing an outcome. The speaker expressly calls the opportunity risky, identifies STRONG-price volatility, says a possible reward-decay model remains unconfirmed, and states that the material is not financial advice. Those warnings matter because the dollar figures are framed conditionally: the speaker says results change with the token price and number of nodes, and describes the figures as potential rather than certain. A viewer is therefore given material risk information alongside the upside discussion, which is more consistent with cautious investment commentary than a deceptive promise.

there's no nothing factual on that yet so it's still up in the air
none of this is financial advice.
these numbers all change also depending how many nodes you buy and depending on what the price of strong is when you first invest into it

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing account emphasizes the attractive figures but omits that the speaker expressly labels the activity risky and says crypto outcomes can change. The cited setup costs and fees establish expense, not deception; the reward-decay claim is presented as an unverified rumor, not concealed adverse information. The presence of conditional projections and an explicit financial-advice disclaimer makes the presentation materially different from a guaranteed-return pitch.

citations.quote: of course it's crypto guys you know anything could happen with crypto
recent rumors about a decaying model for rewards

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Warnings do not neutralize the central solicitation. The video still pairs those qualifications with a concrete path to purchase, recurring fees, and large projected earnings. The speaker says the material is intended to help viewers set up nodes, while the disclaimer merely distances the speaker from financial-advice responsibility. Calling rewards potential or conditional does not change that the presentation encourages viewers to fund the system and compound into more nodes.

as long as i compound my rewards every time i get 10 strong i create a brand new node
you have to pay a monthly maintenance fee to keep your node running which is 1495 and that's every single month

opening.argument: The video's primary format is instructional and demonstrative. It explains what nodes are, distinguishes them from miners, describes the stated protocol purpose, walks through buying STRONG and transferring it to MetaMask, and then shows how to create a node. The speaker also grounds the discussion in personal experience, saying what he has done and plans to do, rather than presenting himself as certifying an inevitable result. A tutorial that explains an operational process and illustrates a personal calculation is reasonably classified as technology education or a demonstration, even where the subject involves financial risk.

citations.quote: A node is basically a computer that connects to a cryptocurrency network.
now you've bought your strong you've set up your meta mask you've added the strong coin on your meta mask
then just fill out no name and no description
This is just my experience, what I plan on doing, what I'm currently doing to try to make some passive income

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing account treats every instructional step as solicitation, but describing wallet setup and node creation is also exactly what an operational tutorial does. The speaker explains the underlying technology before giving steps and identifies the calculations as his own experience and plan. The existence of a purchase step does not by itself establish that the video's primary purpose is deceptive promotion rather than demonstrating how the service works.

citations.quote: Nodes store and transmit data that is bundled together in a block hence the name blockchain
This is just my experience, what I plan on doing, what I'm currently doing to try to make some passive income

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The tutorial framing is inseparable from the investment pitch: the explanation culminates in instructions to buy tokens, fund ETH gas, pay the fee, and create a node. The speaker does not merely demonstrate neutral software operation; he presents his own earnings and urges viewers toward the same setup. Technical vocabulary and step-by-step instructions describe the mechanism but do not remove the financial solicitation.

citations.quote: create a node you need ten strong so at current prices that's about four thousand seven hundred and fifty dollars for one node
Also you need to have some Ethereum in your wallet To cover the gas fees
Now go to StrongBlocks.com Then Hit Create Your Node

opening.argument: On the supplied evidence, this looks like a disclosed purchase of access to an external hosted service, not a hidden scam mechanism. The speaker explains that StrongBlock hosts and maintains the node, identifies the ten-STRONG contribution and monthly maintenance fee, and shows how the contribution is distributed. The material does not establish a downline, credential harvesting, guaranteed return, or secret deposit scheme. It also expressly warns that failure to pay can result in losing the node and investment, and that distribution can change. Those disclosed commercial terms support treating this as a risky service purchase rather than inferring fraud from the existence of fees.

citations.quote: what strong block basically does is they host and maintain the node for you
a node this is how you do it. First you have to buy strong
you have to pay a monthly maintenance fee to keep your node running which is 1495 and that's every single month

rebuttal.rebuttal: The evidence shows an ordinary paid service with disclosed costs and operational consequences, not the missing hallmarks of a scam. A contribution and recurring fee can be contractual pricing for hosted infrastructure. The opposing account calls the contribution non-refundable and emphasizes rewards, but it does not show a downline, a credential request, or a guaranteed return; it therefore asks the judge to infer the mechanism rather than identify it.

citations.quote: here's a breakdown of exactly how your contribution of 10 strong to the strong block community is distributed

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The service label does not resolve the core issue: participation requires purchasing STRONG and making a non-refundable contribution, followed by ongoing payment to preserve access, while rewards are tied to that contribution. The video itself says the initial investment funds rewards and promotes compounding into additional nodes. Whether there is a downline or credential request is beside the point when the relevant paid-node return mechanism is directly shown.

citations.quote: The investment that we make to create a new node is basically how the rewards get paid out
